clue.text: Look during ancient times at group of nations

indicators.note: the look word sits during, that is within, the abbreviation for the ancient era

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks dates in ancient times
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: An instruction to study a historical alliance of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries acting together politically.

clue.text: It is used in hunting deer that are fiery

parts.note: bucks are male deer
hot means fiery

explanation.surface: Something used when hunting lively deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is coarse lead shot fired from shotguns at game.

clue.text: Removed grey coat from class

indicators.note: the letters of grey coat are moved about, removed from their order, into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone took off a grey coat as they left the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as taking a coat off, but it signals the letters of GREY COAT being moved again.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or grouping of things sharing features.

clue.text: Sour part of the milk production?

definitions.text: Sour part of the milk production?

parts.words: Sour part of the milk production?
parts.note: the compound made as milk sours, responsible for its sharp taste, read as a chemistry puzzle

explanation.surface: A question about what makes milk go sour.
explanation.definitionFit: This acid forms when bacteria ferment milk sugar, giving soured milk its tang.

clue.text: Recently after which play was taken off

definitions.text: after which play was taken off

explanation.surface: A theatre show closed recently.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means yesterday evening, i.e. recently, and also the final performance of a run, after which a show closes.

clue.text: Tidied up on board?

parts.note: read literally as sailors clearing a ship's planked floors; idiomatically, preparing by getting obstacles out of the way

explanation.surface: Someone tidied up aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means removing clutter before action, originally clearing a warship's floors before battle.

clue.text: Nearly completely?

parts.note: a close shave is nearly total; something done in a near or tight way, and thoroughly, as in watched carefully

explanation.surface: A question asking whether something is almost total.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb can mean near in distance and also thoroughly or carefully, as in studied minutely.

clue.text: Exciting but second cheerleader leaves, it is to do with the weather

definitions.text: it is to do with the weather

indicators.note: the cheerleader letter leaves, dropping out of the word for exciting

parts.note: climactic means reaching an exciting peak
the leader of cheer is C; second picks the second C in the longer word

explanation.surface: A cheerleader quits, making things exciting, and the topic turns to the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the second C from CLIMACTIC leaves the weather word; the two are often confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-term weather of a region.

clue.text: Number said in France to include soldier

indicators.note: the French word is made to include the soldier, which goes inside it

parts.note: dit is French for said
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A number reported in France includes a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral from nought to nine.

clue.text: Prickly plant jaggedly cut sack almost completely

indicators.note: cut jaggedly, the letters are hacked about into a new order
almost means the word sack loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A spiky plant tore a rough slit almost all along a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' trims SACK to SAC; 'jaggedly' rearranges CUT and SAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny succulent of desert regions.

clue.text: Showing up former sitting

parts.note: ex means former
posing for a portrait is sitting for it

explanation.surface: Someone exposes a former partner sitting for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing means revealing or unmasking someone, showing them up.

clue.text: Hit on a new rallying cry

parts.note: slog means hit hard

explanation.surface: A batter hits out at a fresh motto.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchphrase used to rally support.

clue.text: Pertinent about eastern Mediterranean

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the Levant is the region of the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Something is relevant regarding the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means bearing on the matter in hand, to the point.

clue.text: Stiffness of one remarkably tidy outfit first

indicators.note: first means the outfit word is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: rig means an outfit of clothes or gear
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of tidy are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: How stiff a neat outfit looks when worn first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' rearranges TIDY to DITY; 'first' puts RIG in front of I and DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity is inflexibility, the quality of not bending.

clue.text: Dog-end on table on back of lorry

parts.note: the end of a dog is its tail
board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A cigarette stub left on a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog-end' is British slang for a cigarette butt, but here it is read as a dog's end. A LORRY is a British truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailboard is the hinged board closing the rear of a truck or cart.

clue.text: Shallow container rector found in waterway

indicators.note: the abbreviation is found in the river name, sitting inside it

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A vicar discovers a shallow dish in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The TAY is the longest river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat, shallow holder with raised edges for carrying things.

clue.text: Three-quarters of the sea before one's continent has been lost

indicators.note: before means the trimmed ocean comes ahead of the next piece
three-quarters of the ocean name keeps six of its eight letters, the rest dropped

parts.note: the Atlantic is an ocean
one's is I's, read as I plus S

explanation.surface: A tale of most of the ocean sitting before a vanished landmass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters of' drops IC from ATLANTIC to leave ATLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island continent said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: The lowest film, but it's found on top

definitions.text: film, but it's found on top

explanation.surface: A low-grade movie that still tops the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowlifes are called the dregs of society; the word also means a frothy layer of impurity floating on a liquid.

clue.text: Aware feeling excluded large number

indicators.note: excluded means the number letter is left out of the word for feeling

parts.note: sentiment means a feeling
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A conscious emotion kept out a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and feel, conscious.

clue.text: Animal is redrawn on large canvas sheet

indicators.note: redrawn means the letters of animal is are sketched out again in a new order

explanation.surface: An animal is painted again on a big canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' looks like an artist's, but it is sailcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsail is the principal sail of a ship, made of canvas.

clue.text: Out of sorts titmice harbouring first parasite

indicators.note: out of sorts suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged
first takes the opening letter of harbouring

explanation.surface: Unwell tits are hosting a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives H, the opening letter of 'harbouring', which joins TITMICE before 'Out of sorts' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: The itch mite is a tiny arachnid that burrows into skin, causing scabies.

clue.text: Like an island ignorant of other people's cultures

explanation.surface: Islanders cut off from other cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin insula, island, and also means narrow-minded and uninterested in outsiders.

clue.text: Les faxed about source of oil

indicators.note: about means the letters of Les faxed are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Les sent a fax concerning an oil supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil is pressed from the seeds of the flax plant.

clue.text: Renowned football body going over sea shortly

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
Med is the short name for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Football's governing body is well known for heading to the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed means celebrated, widely known.

clue.text: Even so can interrupt

parts.note: but means even so or however
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, it is possible to cut in.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to interrupt or intrude on a conversation.

clue.text: Harsh-sounding, tinny perhaps

explanation.surface: A sound that is grating and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a hard, clanging sound, and also anything made of metal, of which tin is an example.

clue.text: Sacred writings from a Roman goddess

parts.note: Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: Holy texts said to come from a Roman deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the scripture of Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: Last course Sidney returned, much troubled

indicators.note: returned means the pudding and the short name are read backwards as one run

parts.note: dessert is the final course of a meal
Sid is short for Sidney

explanation.surface: Sidney sent his pudding back, very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: DESSERT and SID together, read backwards, give DIS + TRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means deeply upset or anguished.

clue.text: One of the bellringer's duties

parts.note: the slow sounding of a bell, a ringer's task; duties also hints at a charge levied, such as a road fee

explanation.surface: A job a church bellringer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To toll a bell is to ring it slowly and steadily; a toll is also a levy or duty.
